summary: The precision wave kite. Penta TX and Trinity TX materials for exceptional shape retention in powered turns. Hybrid Flex Strut for explosive turning, lightweight trailing edge battens for canopy stability, massive drift for aggressive down-the-line surfing.
best_for: Precision wave riding and strapless freestyle

sources.summary: The SLS materials take the Neo to another level. Shape retention in powered turns is exceptional and the drift is world-class. The Hybrid Flex Strut delivers explosive redirects.
If you're a serious wave rider and budget isn't the top concern, the Neo SLS over the standard Neo is worth every penny.

reviews.full_transcript: Make it loud. >> [music] [music] >> Heat. Heat. >> [music] [music] >> Today we have the Duoone Neo SLS, Duo Tone's classic wave kite in our test. Of course, this is a fully matured kite and has been for quite some time, but small details like the slightly rounder tip segments can also be found in the 2026 model, as well as a four-point bridal with a pulley that supports the front tube. The steering lines are attached to a V bungee, which also features three different color-coded points to adjust bar pressure and turning speed. The short bridle only requires line deflectors on the front tube. The three central cross struts do without them. For the canopy, Duatone uses the proven combination of triple and double riptop material. The only change throughout the entire kite is at the trailing edge. At the rear edge where we use a high strength double riptop material for inflation and deflation, there is a large inlet and outlet valve. The one pump system is very short and completely straight. If you don't want to deflate your kite towards the center, but rather towards one of the tip ends, there's an additional dump valve on one side for that purpose. The material used in the SLS variants from Duo Tone is a high strength dacron with a large grid reinforcement of polyester threads. The front tube is sealed here with a simple kadar seam which is doubled and stitched from the inside. The cross struts are each attached to the canopy with a single seam and are doubled and glued from the inside. And to make sure nothing flutters at the trailing edge, there are also two additional bats on each side. All impact and abrasion points are reinforced with a rubberized fabric and the central part features a large triangle made of SLS material. And at the transition from the front tube to the canopy, the whole thing is further adorned with a slightly wider fabric reinforcement. Thanks to a highly efficient combination of strong baseline pull for a wave kite, very effective acceleration through a gentle sign curve, and the beautifully and quickly attached air flow, you get really excellent performance when getting up to speed. Even in slightly underpowered conditions where the wind is a bit offshore and you really have to actively work the bar quite a bit, you can still manage to get out of the wave setup very smoothly and quite evenly. And that in turn provides a significant amount of extra safety that you can readily gain here. >> Depending on how far I place the knot or loop on the bungee towards the outside, the more pronounced the windward behavior becomes. Overall, in all three aspects, there is very good upwind performance here thanks to the small front tube diameter, low resistance, and a very efficient upwind run. When it comes to bar feeling, the new North SLS is truly something special. We have a kite that responds very quickly and very sensitively to every steering command. But on the other hand, it also has such a stable positioning, especially when it comes to drift. That's really quite exceptional. And of course, the positioning is also influenced by the steering line attachment. If you leave it in the middle setting, you get medium, truly medium steering and holding forces. If you move a bit further inward, closer to the center of the kite, you can increase these forces slightly. This makes the kite even more stable. So, for those who want to drift, that's a really good thing. And for those who want a more responsive, actively steered experience, you can also try setting it all the way to the outside. As mentioned, the basic pull is very strong. However, thanks to the kite's absolutely efficient DEP power performance, you can always regulate and control it very precisely. And something similar applies to the way the power develops. The power delivery is already a bit explosive, which will of course excite those who like to use it for jumping. But for surfing in the waves, you naturally want a calmer and more consistent power delivery from the kite. And once it's positioned, it delivers that 100%. The canopy truly just stays in one designated spot so easily. It absolutely doesn't act up at all and consistently gives you a feeling of complete and utter safety. But if responsiveness is required in the next situation, it reacts super quickly and precisely to steering commands. It really picks up speed even at high-flying speeds. But the feedback you get from the bar and what the kite delivers to the bar is so precise that you know exactly when pull is about to build up and you need to depower a little more to relieve the pressure. When it comes to flight characteristics we actually have to talk about two different types. On the one hand, we have this absolutely calm and incredibly reliable behavior, but on the other hand, there's also a really tight turning ability with super tight, fully rounded turns, which can also result in high flight speeds. Thanks to the fine tuning of the Duo Tone Neo SLS, it's really just a matter of what each person wants in a given situation. With this kite, you definitely get both. And each one is delivered in a truly 100% pure, optimal, and clean form. The Neo Sl226 is really well suited for every area in the waves, no matter what you want to do. Do you want it to be fast, responsive, and powerful? Or do you just want it to stand docsile in one position, stoically waiting for you to finish a wave? Accordingly, the question is which style you prefer with this kite? Because both styles, whether actively steered or set and left, are catered to perfectly, 100%. When it comes to drift, we have to say clearly that in our opinion, it's currently almost unique. The kite's geometry is spot on here, and the suspension is just right. So, you can definitely say this is a very well-rounded and harmonious kite concept for wave riding. The only objection you might raise is that depending on personal preference, you might want to attach the steering lines a bit further in from the center or just leave them at the center. But that's really just a matter of personal taste. And in fact, it's almost more of a feature of this kite, allowing you to better accommodate your preferred style because what happens when you attach the steering lines a bit further out or a bit further in, is of course that it affects where the kite positions itself in the wind window. If you fly it with the lines attached further in, the kite is overall more stable. In very strong gusty winds, you can control the kite even better this way. It also remains even more stable in its position and simply can't fly as far forward anymore. If you need it for a more actively steered style or in strong side offshore winds where the kite should be as far forward in the wind window as possible and remain highly responsive, then you attach the lines further out accordingly. That was basically just an additional explanation on the side, but of course in the end every kite does that. But with the Neo SLS, you really get two slightly different feelings. For us, the Datan Neo SLS is definitely the best Neo that Datan has built so far because both flavors or both different variants can be presented 100% in one kite. In any case, that's a lot of money overall. On the other hand, you definitely get pure joy for wave riding in return.
reviews.summary: Gleiten tv gave the Neo SLS 2026 a thorough technical and on-water assessment, praising its near-unique drift stability and its ability to switch between docile park-and-wait behavior and tight, fast turning depending on bridle setting. They highlighted the three-position V-bungee steering attachment as a meaningful tuning tool and noted strong upwind performance. The only reservation raised was the high price point of €1,919 for the 7m.

structured_review.summary: The Duotone Neo SLS 2026 is a wave kite that excels at doing two things simultaneously: parking with exceptional drift stability and turning with tight, fast, responsive arcs. Its tri-point steering line attachment system lets riders dial in bar pressure and turning speed to match their style, making it genuinely versatile across wave conditions. The only real caveat is the premium price tag, which demands serious commitment from the buyer.
pros: Exceptional drift — reviewers called it near-unique in its ability to hold position while the rider surfs the wave
Three color-coded steering line attachment points allow meaningful customization of bar pressure and turning speed
Strong upwind performance aided by small front tube diameter and low drag
Power delivery that is explosive when needed but smooth and consistent once parked
Tight, fast turning with fully rounded arcs at high kite speeds
SLS material construction with extensive reinforcements for durability and shape retention
cons: Explosive power delivery may feel unsettled for pure wave surfers who prefer a calmer, more progressive pull
High price — €1,919 for the 7m tested — a significant investment
Bar pressure and drift behavior require some personal tuning via the bridle settings to find the ideal setup
structured_review.best_for: Intermediate to advanced wave riders who want a kite that drifts exceptionally well down the line but can also be actively driven through tight turns when needed.
structured_review.not_for: Budget-conscious riders or beginners who won't exploit the precision tuning options and nuanced wave performance this kite demands.
structured_review.rec_blurb: Unmatched drift and surgical turns in one kite — the wave specialist that does both perfectly.
